title: Where your $25 T-shirt money goes
hook_variants: This shirt cost about two dollars to make. You paid twenty-five.
You paid twenty-five dollars for two dollars of T-shirt.
Somebody made twenty-three dollars off your T-shirt. Let's find them.

scenes.say: This shirt cost about two dollars to make. You paid twenty-five.
So who took the other twenty-three? Let's follow the money.
Cotton and sewing in Bangladesh. Then a container ship. Then a port. Then a truck to the store.
Shipping it across the ocean? Around ten cents. Not a typo.
scenes.label: OCEAN SHIPPING PER SHIRT

scenes.say: Make it, two dollars. Ship and tariff, about two. The brand takes around six. The store takes the rest.
The most expensive part of your shirt is the shelf it hangs on.
Follow Landed Costs. I show you what things really cost.

caption:
Your $25 T-shirt costs about $2 to make. The ocean crossing? Around 10 cents. So where does the rest go? 👕🚢
